6 March, 2026

In The High Court For The State Of Telangana
 At Hyderabad
 The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Tirumala Devi Eada
 Criminal Petition No.7738 of 2022
 Date Of Order:06.03.2026
Between:
Syed Ameenullah Husaini @ Saber & 4 others
 ...Petitioners/Accused Nos.2 to 6
And
The State of Telangana,
rep. by its Public Prosecutor and another.

High Court For The State Of Telangana
 At Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
...Respondents
 Order

1. This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of The Code of Criminal Procedure (for short,
'Cr.P.C) seeking to quash the proceedings against the petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 6 in C.C.No.681 of 2016, on the file of the learned XIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 406 of IPC and Sections 4 & 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

entities.text: XIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The de-facto complainant/respondent No.2 herein filed a complaint before the police on 04.09.2014 stating that her marriage with the petitioner/A1 was performed on 03.06.2012 at ETD,J Crl.P.No.7738_2022 Hyderabad and at the time of marriage, cash, gold, silver ornaments and jahez articles were given as dowry as per the custom.
After one month of the marriage, the petitioner/A1 and other accused started subjecting the de-facto complainant to harassment.

During the course of such harassment, A3 beat her on her head and demanded to bring Rs.5 lakhs as additional dowry,
alleging that the dowry, which was given earlier, was very less.

In the month of February, 2013,
again the demand for Rs.5 lakhs was reiterated stating that the accused No.1 required the said amount for arranging VISA.
With great difficulty, the de-facto complainant's mother and brother have arranged Rs.2 lakhs.
On 06.03.2013, A1 and A2 picked up quarrel with the de-facto complainant, A3 to A5 have dragged her holding her clothes, A4 beat her with hands on her neck and A5 beat her with slipper.
Meanwhile, A1 also inflicted a blow on her abdomen ignoring that she was pregnant.

On the strength of her complaint a case in Crime No.272 of 2014 for the offence under Sections 498(A) and 406 IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act was registered and after completion of investigation, charge sheet was filed against the accused and the same is taken on filed as C.C.No.681 of 2016.
The present petition is filed to quash ETD,J Crl.P.No.7738_2022

sentences.text: 1 C.C.No.681 of 2016 on the ground that the divorce has been taken by accused No.1 with the de-facto complainant as per Islamic law on 24.10.2018 and that even as per the charge sheet there are no grounds for prosecuting the accused
. Prior to filing of this petition, O.P.No.1185 of 2015 was filed for grant of mutual consent divorce on the file of Family Court, City Civil Court, Hyderabad.
A Memorandum of Compromise was recorded by the learned Family Court, Hyderabad.
One of the clauses in the said Memorandum of Compromise is that all the cases filed in various Courts by both the parties will be withdrawn.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has placed reliance on an authority decided by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajiv Kumar Sharma and another vs.
The State of Uttar Pradesh and another 1, wherein, at paragraphs 6 and 7, it is held as under:
"6.

The State of Uttar Pradesh and another 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that after the settlement, matrimonial proceedings have been finally disposed of.
The High Court despite this arrangement arrived at between the parties, however, declined to quash the proceedings.

In our opinion, the High Court should have taken note of the fact that the parties have amicably resolved all their differences and consciously chose to unconditionally drop all further proceedings related to Criminal Appeal No.1599 of 2019, dated 21.10.2019 ETD,J Crl.P.No.7738_2022 marriage inter se including the criminal action initiated by the complainant-respondent No.2.
7.

Accordingly, in the interest of justice and additionally in exercise of powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, we set aside the impugned judgment of the High Court and also quash the complaint case No.1229 of 2015 (Smt. Anupam Vs.
Rajeev Sharma and others), pending before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kasganj."
3.

Rajeev Sharma and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The petitioner has also filed memorandum of compromise, wherein paragraph 3 shows that C.C.No.681 of 2016 on the file of the XIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court,
Hyderabad, is also agreed to be withdrawn by respondent No.2.

entities.text:
XIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court,
Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 admitted that there was a settlement between the parties and that both the parties have agreed to withdraw all the matters pending in various Courts.
However he has submitted that accused No.1 still has to pay an amount of Rs.75,000/- to the de-facto complainant and also has to pay some maintenance amount towards her child.

5. Learned counsel for petitioners submitted that accused No.1 had already handed over original demand draft dated 10.06.2022 for Rs.75,000/- to the de-facto complainant in the ETD,J Crl.P.No.7738_2022 open Court in Crl.P.No 673 of 2019, dated 16.06.2021 and filed photocopy of the demand draft in the Court, which shows that a demand draft was drawn in favour of the de-facto complainant through Axis Bank for a sum of Rs.75,000/-.
Learned counsel for the petitioners also submitted that the petitioners are ready to pay the arrears of maintenance to the child of the de-facto complainant, as agreed, in installments.

6. Considering the circumstances explained above, including the clause in the Memorandum of Compromise executed by both the parties to withdraw C.C.No.681 of 2016 pending on the file of XIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Hyderabad, and also taking into consideration Syed Ameenullah Husaini , Saber vs The State Of Telangana on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92313440/
2 that the other terms of Memorandum of Understanding are complied with, the fact that Rs.75,000/-, which was to be paid by the petitioners in favour of respondent No.2, was paid by way of demand draft in the open Court and also considering the fact that the petitioners have agreed to pay the arrears of maintenance to the child of the de- facto complainant in installments, this Court is of the opinion that the case against the petitioners in C.C.No.681 of 2016 can be quashed.

8. Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
